nodes.title: Integral section model
nodes.statement: Given a reduced proper rigid X over an algebraically closed complete K, a line bundle L and a finite affinoid cover U_i=Spa(R_i,R_i°) with affinoid intersections, choose sections s_j^(i). Require s_i^(i) to frame L, all ratios s_j^(i)/s_i^(i) to be power bounded, U_ij to be the unit locus of s_j^(i)/s_i^(i), and overlap differences divided by a frame to have norm at most |ϖ|. Transport the general formal gluing construction to these actual rings: 𝔛 has charts Spf R_i°, its generic fibre is X, and 𝔏 has integral frame s_i^(i). The sections reduce to global s̄_j modulo ϖ. The charts are D(s̄_i); 𝔛 is projective and 𝔏 ample. The structure sheaf on each chart is the power-bounded ring, with ϖ-completed localization on intersections.
hypotheses: 0≠ϖ∈𝔪_K; integral rings are R_i° rather than arbitrary plus rings.
On U_ik the overlap congruence is measured using s_i^(i); finite cover and reducedness are essential.
proofSteps: For J⊂J′ localize at the product of ratios indexed by J′\J, then complete; invoke formal gluing and its generic-fibre comparison.
Glue frame transition units; the overlap congruences glue the reduced sections.

After its quantified quotient A→A/I with I^(4(d+1))=0, four action/characteristic calculations agree: (1) the ambient Shimura finite-level support diagram, fixed-exponent completion and almost boundary-ideal Čech comparison followed by classical section approximation; (2) the ambient boundary action on the GL_n interior image through unnormalized Levi Satake; (3) auxiliary-character Laurent realization and degree-n determinant extraction; (4) the integral GL_n spherical polynomial from IHG.3 after reciprocal/geometric-Frobenius and ε⁻¹ transport. The common value at every v∉S is P_v in (A/I)[X]. For a full ordinary GL_n finite-level module with coefficients M_ξ/p^m, apply these squares to its interior and lower-rank boundary subquotients, then glue by TC.4 boundary induction and the assembly quotient I^N=0, N=N([F:Q],n). The squares commute under ring base change and coefficient/level pullback/trace on joint quotients. Almost errors in route (1) are discharged by finite-coefficient faithfulness; the nilpotent ideal is a separate error.
hypotheses: These are maps of actions and characteristic coefficients, not a purported canonical map taking an arbitrary cohomology class to a polynomial.
Agreement under a coefficient or level change is stated only after the named common quotient maps, not by inventing A_m→A_r.

The perfectoid comparison is on the ambient Hodge-type Shimura tower. There is no asserted perfectoid compactification or direct class-to-section map for an arbitrary GL_n locally symmetric space. For full ordinary cohomology compare the action on its specified filtration subquotients, not a claimed lift of each class to the ambient tower.
proofSteps: Use the Siegel boundary annihilator containment to connect the GL_n interior image with the ambient Shimura action; compose that ambient finite-level support/trace diagram with TC.2 comparison and continuity. Keep exponent 4(d+1) on the extracted interior quotient.
Compose boundary Satake and character-twist identities with the extracted determinant characteristic formula.
Use determinant uniqueness on dense Frobenius data and the IHG base-change maps to identify the two composites on each common coefficient quotient.

For ordinary coefficients descend and filter through the interior and smaller-Levi boundary modules; compare each graded action square and use the uniform assembly ideal I^N=0 rather than asserting a perfectoid map on GL_n classes.

nodes.title: Residual and local specialization
nodes.statement: A finite-field Hecke eigensystem on the finite torsion module kills the nilpotent ideal, so IHG reconstruction supplies a continuous semisimple degree-n representation over an algebraic closure with characteristic P_v; it is unique up to conjugacy. For an absolutely irreducible residual system over a finite extension k/F_p, the completed local integral Hecke image at that system is a complete henselian finite O-algebra. The supplied determinant and IHG absolutely irreducible reconstruction yield an actual representation over it, with characteristic polynomial expressed using its Hecke-image eigenvalue map. After fixing a residual basis its uniqueness is up to strict conjugacy, not literal equality. Semisimple mod-p existence does not imply an arbitrary reducible integral representation lift.
hypotheses: The finite field contains the eigensystem; absolute irreducibility is tested after algebraic closure.
Use the correct eigenvalue map of the local Hecke image, not the unrelated original field-valued ψ in the source misprint.
proofSteps: Factor the field-valued map through the nilpotent quotient.
Invoke existing IHG residual semisimple specialization and characteristic uniqueness.
In the absolutely irreducible local case invoke the supplied henselian reconstruction and quotient lifting theorem.

nodes.title: Rank one and two normalization checks
nodes.statement: For GL₁, with geometric reciprocity, an unramified finite-order class-field character ψ evaluated by the standard double-coset U₁ gives P_v=1−q_vψ(Frob_v)X. The Scholze-normalized output is ε⁻¹ψ, while the standard reciprocal convention gives ψ. For GL₂ over Q on modular-curve cohomology, with integral double-coset eigenvalues t_ℓ,d_ℓ, IHG’s monic polynomial is Y²−t_ℓY+ℓd_ℓ, its reciprocal is 1−t_ℓX+ℓd_ℓX², and the Scholze polynomial is 1−ℓt_ℓX+ℓ³d_ℓX². Validate the four-route theorem by this ε⁻¹ twist and by inverse Frobenius conversion when using arithmetic Frobenius. These are normalization tests of supplied class-field/modular objects, not additional constructions of them.
hypotheses: ℓ∉S and ℓ≠p so all powers are units in the coefficient ring.
U_i are the standard double-coset generators; they are not the normalized e_i.
proofSteps: Apply the exact e_i versus U_i identity of TC.3.
Check rank one with global/local reciprocity and ε(Frob_geom)=q⁻¹.

nodes.title: Arithmetic nonlifting check
nodes.statement: Take F=Q,n=1,p=2,K=Ẑˣ and the trivial integral coefficient lattice. With the source’s stack convention the arithmetic quotient is [point/{±1}]. Its H¹ with Z₂ coefficients is zero, but H¹ with F₂ coefficients is F₂ and its Bockstein maps isomorphically to H²(Z₂)[2]. Thus this actual arithmetic torsion class has no integral H¹ lift. At every odd ℓ the rank-one tame generator acts as identity and the extracted mod-2 determinant is trivial, since q_ℓ≡1 mod2. The universal coefficient diagram still commutes and the simultaneous finite-coefficient kernel is contained in the integral kernel. As a separate algebraic diagnostic, the two-term integral complex Z --2→ Z has a mod-2 degree-zero class 1 with no integral degree-zero lift.
hypotheses: Do not silently replace the nonneat stack quotient by its coarse point, which loses the class.
The two-term complex diagnostic supplements rather than replaces the arithmetic example.
proofSteps: Identify Qˣ\(Rˣ/(R_>0·{±1})×A_fˣ/Ẑˣ) with the single orbit and stabilizer {±1}.
Compute cyclic group cohomology via the alternating zero/multiplication-by-2 resolution and its Bockstein.
Evaluate odd-prime GL₁ Hecke action and the character polynomial; compare with UCT and all four routes.
